cover.title: TimescaleDB Design System
cover.categories: Design System, Visual Design, UI, UX

header: TimescaleDB brings the power of PostgreSQL to time-series data. Our design system matches that technical strength. We built a clear, structured framework that respects deep technical work while making complex ideas easy to see. This visual system signals to every developer: this is for you.

layout.title: The Design Philosophy
text: Developer tools exist in a visual paradox: they must feel powerful without being intimidating, and technical without being sterile. We started by studying how developers interact with documentation and dashboards. They don’t want decoration; they want clarity. We built this system to achieve three goals: visualize abstract data, maintain technical credibility, and scale across every touchpoint.

layout.title: Color & Accessibility
text: We built the color palette around high-contrast accessibility and the specific needs of data visualization. A primary gold grounds the brand in warmth while staying professional. Banner blue and navy provide a technical backbone, while extended scales offer the flexibility needed for complex UI states and dense data.

layout.title: Visual Narrative
text: Our illustration style uses isometric perspective and technical line work to turn abstract concepts into tangible ideas. We transformed hypertables, data retention, and time-series architecture into visual narratives rather than documentation hurdles. This approach bridges the gap between deep code and quick understanding.

layout.title: Interface & Workflow
text: Every UI element supports the developer workflow. Form fields, buttons, and interactive states follow familiar patterns while maintaining a distinct point of view. Spacing is precise, states are comprehensive, and nothing is decorative. Every pixel serves a functional purpose.

layout.title: Consistency Across the Experience
text: Avatars and spot illustrations extend this system across the entire journey. They maintain a consistent voice while adapting to different contexts, from the deep product experience to high-level marketing.
The result is a design system that feels like it was built by people who actually use databases. Because it was.
